The light of dusk filtered into the yard through the trees
on the ridge. Claire wedged herself into the bay window by
the porch and reread Gramma Adie’s letter. The hand that
wrote it was visibly rheumatic. The d’s and t’s were gangly
and the s’s were pinched, telling more about Gramma’s
condition than the words themselves. Claire’s memory of
her grandmother had faded in the last two years. She had
trouble holding the image in her head, She could clearly see
an ever-twitching cheek and she could hear the old woman
cough, but Claire had to struggle to remember what color her
eyes were, She didn’t even remember’ whether she had glasses

oF not,

Before she got the TB, Gramma Adie had gone to
Missouri to help out her eldest granddaughter—
cousin Joann. The divorce happened shortly after that when
Gramma found a Northern man who promised to take care
of her. Claire thought that was nice of the Northemer, but
ipa had a lot of words for the man, even though he and
Gramma busted up pretty quick. Now, Gramma was back
in Joann’s house and Joann still had plenty of trouble with
her two kids to worry about a sickly old woman.
